text: The $\textbf{Great Wall of China}$ was primarily built to protect the Chinese states from invasions by which group?
explanation: Construction began as early as the 7th century BC, with the most famous sections built by the Ming Dynasty to defend against nomadic northern tribes.

text: Which city-state in ancient Greece is credited with introducing the concept of $\textbf{Democracy}$?
explanation: In the 5th century BC, Athens developed a system where eligible citizens could vote directly on legislation.

text: Who was the Macedonian king who created one of the largest empires in the ancient world, stretching from Greece to India?
explanation: Tutored by Aristotle, Alexander remained undefeated in battle and spread Hellenistic culture throughout his empire.

text: The $\textbf{Ides of March}$ (44 BC) marks the assassination of which Roman dictator?
explanation: Caesar was stabbed to death by a group of senators, an event that ultimately led to the end of the Roman Republic.

text: The fall of the $\textbf{Western Roman Empire}$ is traditionally dated to which year?
explanation: This year marks the deposition of the last Roman Emperor, Romulus Augustulus, by the Germanic chieftain Odoacer.

text: Which prophet founded the religion of $\textbf{Islam}$ in the 7th century?
explanation: Muhammad united Arabia into a single Muslim polity, with the Quran becoming the central religious text of Islam.

text: Who was crowned $\textbf{Emperor of the Romans}$ on Christmas Day, 800 AD, uniting much of Western Europe?
explanation: Also known as Charles the Great, he was the King of the Franks and laid the foundations for modern France and Germany.

text: The $\textbf{Battle of Hastings}$ in 1066 resulted in the conquest of England by:
explanation: William the Conqueror, Duke of Normandy, defeated King Harold II, changing the course of English history and language.

text: The $\textbf{Magna Carta}$, signed in 1215, is significant because it:
options: Limited the power of the King
Granted women the right to vote
answer: Limited the power of the King
explanation: It established the principle that everyone, including the king, was subject to the law.

text: Which Mongol leader established the largest contiguous land empire in history?
explanation: He united the nomadic tribes of Northeast Asia and launched invasions that conquered vast territories.

text: The $\textbf{Black Death}$ was a pandemic that killed millions in Europe during the:
explanation: Caused by the bacterium *Yersinia pestis*, it is estimated to have killed 30% to 60% of Europe's population.

text: Who was the French heroine of the $\textbf{Hundred Years' War}$ burned at the stake in 1431?
explanation: The 'Maid of Orléans' claimed divine guidance and led the French army to several important victories.

text: Who is credited with inventing the movable-type $\textbf{Printing Press}$ in Europe around 1440?
explanation: His invention revolutionized the spread of information, playing a key role in the Renaissance and Reformation.

text: Which Renaissance artist painted the $\textbf{Mona Lisa}$ and the $\textbf{Last Supper}$?
explanation: Leonardo was a polymath whose notebooks reveal a spirit of scientific inquiry and mechanical inventiveness.

text: The $\textbf{Protestant Reformation}$ began when Martin Luther posted his:
explanation: In 1517, Luther criticized the Catholic Church's sale of indulgences, sparking a religious schism in Europe.

text: Which English King is famous for having six wives and breaking with the Catholic Church?
explanation: He established the Church of England, naming himself its supreme head, to annul his first marriage.

text: The $\textbf{Spanish Armada}$ was defeated by the English navy in 1588 during the reign of:
explanation: The defeat of the Armada prevented a Spanish invasion and is considered one of England's greatest military victories.

text: Which astronomer famously faced the Inquisition for supporting the theory that the $\textbf{Earth revolves around the Sun}$?
explanation: Galileo was tried in 1633 and spent the rest of his life under house arrest for his heliocentric views.

text: Who formulated the $\textbf{Laws of Motion}$ and the Law of Universal Gravitation?
explanation: His work 'Principia Mathematica' (1687) laid the groundwork for classical mechanics.

text: The $\textbf{American Revolution}$ officially began with the 'shot heard 'round the world' at the battles of:
explanation: Fought on April 19, 1775, these were the first military engagements of the American Revolutionary War.

text: The storming of the $\textbf{Bastille}$ in 1789 signaled the start of which revolution?
explanation: The Bastille was a symbol of royal tyranny, and its fall marked a turning point in French history.

text: Which military leader declared himself Emperor of France in 1804?
explanation: Napoleon rose to prominence during the French Revolution and conquered much of Europe before his eventual defeat.

text: The $\textbf{Industrial Revolution}$ began in Great Britain with the development of which engine?
explanation: Improvements to the steam engine by James Watt were critical for powering factories and transport.

text: Who was the President of the United States during the $\textbf{Civil War}$?
explanation: Lincoln led the nation through its greatest moral, constitutional, and political crisis, preserving the Union and abolishing slavery.

text: The $\textbf{Wright Brothers}$ are credited with the first successful powered flight in which year?
explanation: Orville and Wilbur Wright achieved the feat at Kitty Hawk, North Carolina.

text: Which ship famously sank on its maiden voyage in 1912 after hitting an iceberg?
explanation: The luxury liner sank in the North Atlantic, resulting in the deaths of over 1,500 people.

text: The assassination of $\textbf{Archduke Franz Ferdinand}$ in 1914 triggered which conflict?
explanation: His assassination in Sarajevo set off a chain of alliances that dragged the major powers of Europe into war.

text: The $\textbf{Russian Revolution}$ of 1917 was led by which Bolshevik leader?
explanation: Lenin led the overthrow of the Provisional Government and established the world's first communist state.

text: Which amendment to the US Constitution granted $\textbf{women the right to vote}$ in 1920?
explanation: It prohibits the states and the federal government from denying the right to vote to citizens on the basis of sex.

text: The $\textbf{Great Depression}$ was triggered by the stock market crash in:
explanation: The crash on Wall Street led to a decade-long economic downturn that affected the entire world.

text: Who was the dictator of $\textbf{Nazi Germany}$ during World War II?
explanation: Hitler's aggressive foreign policy and antisemitic ideology led to the outbreak of WWII and the Holocaust.

text: The attack on $\textbf{Pearl Harbor}$ in 1941 brought which country into World War II?
explanation: The surprise Japanese attack led the US to declare war on Japan the following day.

text: The systematic persecution and genocide of six million Jews by the Nazi regime is known as:
explanation: It remains one of the darkest chapters in human history.

text: The United States dropped atomic bombs on which two Japanese cities in 1945?
explanation: The bombings led to Japan's unconditional surrender, ending World War II.

text: The term $\textbf{'Iron Curtain'}$ refers to the division of Europe during which period?
explanation: It divided the democratic West from the communist East from 1945 until 1991.

text: Who was the leader of the Indian independence movement known for his philosophy of $\textbf{nonviolent resistance}$?
explanation: Gandhi's methods inspired civil rights movements across the world.

text: Which US President was assassinated in Dallas, Texas, in 1963?
explanation: His assassination was a pivotal moment in 20th-century American history.

text: The $\textbf{Apollo 11}$ mission in 1969 resulted in the first humans walking on:
explanation: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin became the first humans to land on the lunar surface.

text: The $\textbf{Berlin Wall}$ fell in which year, symbolizing the end of the Cold War?
explanation: The fall of the wall paved the way for German reunification and the collapse of the Soviet Union.

text: Who was the first black president of $\textbf{South Africa}$, elected in 1994?
explanation: Mandela spent 27 years in prison for his anti-apartheid activities before leading the country's transition to democracy.
